region: Cutchogue · North Fork of Long Island, New York
about: Lieb Cellars was founded in 1992 on Long Island’s North Fork, about 80 miles east of Manhattan, by Mark and Kathy Lieb. Their winemaker from 1993 on was Russell Hearn, an Australian who also founded Premium Wine Group, the East Coast’s first custom-crush winery, in 2000. In 2023 Hearn and his partners bought Lieb, combined it with Suhru, the label his wife Susan started in 2008, and reopened the Oregon Road tasting room. The estate now operates under the name Rooted North.

The fruit comes from the family’s roughly 50 acres of sustainably farmed vineyards around Cutchogue, which also hold what the winery calls the largest contiguous planting of Pinot Blanc in the country. The 2023 brought back the Lieb Estate Sauvignon Blanc after an eight-year break, made because the team judged the harvest excellent for the grape. After fermentation the wine rested five months on its lees, which adds a little texture and a faint brioche note.

The winery describes gooseberry, ripe grapefruit and lime on the nose, opening toward key lime pie, with a lush palate and crisp acidity that carries through the finish. James Suckling’s team called it balanced, elegant and vibrant, with classic gooseberry and key lime notes. Bone dry and moderate in alcohol, it is built for the table: the winery suggests grilled salmon, roast chicken and mushroom risotto.
